author: Bobby Grayson
description: README Layout rows: | Leanactors/Replay.lean | Executable front end to run/runSys (lean_exe replay): a line script on stdin (deliver/run/signal/down/timer), the final observables of bank or ttl in a canonical text form; a disabled choice is an error, not a silent stop | and | elixir/fuzz.exs | Differential fuzz: seeded random phase scripts replayed by .lake/build/bin/replay and by the real modules on the BEAM, outputs compared byte for byte; exits 1 with the script on the first mismatch (--seed S --only N reproduces one run) |. README paragraph (after the drivers / before Build): **Differential testing.** lakefile.toml has a second target, the executable replay (Leanactors/Replay.lean, built by plain lake build), which reads a scheduler script from stdin, drives Bank.beh through run and Ttl.beh/sig through runSys from Bank.init/Ttl.init, and prints the observables the BEAM can also report: for the bank the balance and each client's seen value (none, some v, await) plus the messages left in the mailboxes; for the cache its value (none, some v, dead), the reader's count, every value delivered to the reader in order, and the pending count. elixir/fuzz.exs generates 200 seeded scripts (even runs bank, odd runs ttl), runs each through replay (a Port with the script on stdin) and on the BEAM by driving elixir/src/bank.ex and ttl.ex with the same messages in the same order, and stops at the first difference. Scripts are built from phases that have one outcome under any scheduler, so the BEAM's own scheduling cannot diverge from the Lean schedule: bank casts (FIFO to one process) then run 0 per cast, a tick/audit/double-tick to one client with its fixed run sequence (only one actor has mail at each step, or the one choice is confluent), synchronised on the BEAM with :sys.get_state; for the cache put x (run 0), ask to the reader (run 1, run 0, run 1, synchronised by tracing the reader's receives), expire (Lean fires the live timer, always the last pending one; the BEAM sleeps 300ms past the 200ms TTL; a second expiry is unobservable), stale timers (Lean only, must be no-ops), and put 0 as a terminal phase only, because a send to a dead registered name raises on the BEAM where the model drops it. check.sh runs elixir elixir/fuzz.exs --seed 1 --runs 200 (about 19s, most of it the 300ms expiry sleeps); the two BEAM-side mutants tried (withdraw guard n < b, a cache that keeps its value on expiry) are each caught on the first affected script. README Build block: add 'elixir elixir/fuzz.exs --seed 1 --runs 200   # exits 1 on the first Lean/BEAM mismatch, with the script'. Status line: 'a randomized differential test replays seeded scripts through the Lean interpreters and the BEAM and compares the observables'. NOTES section 10 paragraph: Round 5 added a second use of the executable interpreters: until now run/runSys only produced the #eval traces the drivers compared by hand (bank.exs against snapshot final 3). The replay executable makes any schedule replayable from outside and fuzz.exs generates them. The interesting design question was what a BEAM twin can legitimately be compared to: a Lean schedule is one interleaving, the BEAM picks its own, so the generator only emits confluent phases and the twin waits for each to finish (get_state for GenServers, a receive trace for the raw reader, a monitor for the crash). Two divergences were found by thinking rather than by the fuzzer, both already listed under 'Not modelled': registered names are constant pids (a send to the dead cache raises on the BEAM, so put 0 is terminal) and timers are untimed (expiry is a sleep on the BEAM; stale timers exist only in the model). Both are constraints on the generator, not on the comparison. Line counts: Replay.lean ~235 lines, fuzz.exs ~450 lines.
